text.p: Investors should buy shares of Polish trader Krakchemia SA, which should be buoyed by its income-generating supermarkets placed in strategic locations, the brokerage unit of Bank Handlowy SA said in a report.

"The possession of supermarkets in attractive locations, as well as their effective use as sources of substanital income, has a significant present value which, in our opinion, is not reflected in the company's current net profit," the report dated January 16 said.
On that day Krakchemia closed at 4.85 zlotys and on Monday closed at 5.75 zlotys.
Handlowy said shares of Krakow-based Krakchemia, whose full name is Firma Handlowa Krakchemia SA, also had growth potential over the next three to five years.
The report saw Krakchemia lifting net profit to 1.6 million zlotys this year from one million zlotys in 1996. It said sales would rise to 160 million zlotys from 130 million zlotys.
It saw Krakchemia's price-earnings ratio falling to nine this year from 14.4 in 1996.
Handlowy said a new supermarket gave the firm a strong position in retail sales of food products and industrial articles in and around Krakow, where demand is seen as high.
It said Krakchemia also had a strong wholesale trade position in chemical products and finishing articles for apartments and homes.
But it warned that foreign retail sales chains would provide ever tougher competition.
